```yaml
  include: ["/releases/*", "!/releases/night/*"]
  auth:
    type: sso
    sso:
      startURL: https://acme.awsapps.com/start
      region: eu-west-1
      accountID: "123456789012"
      roleName: ApkReader
      cacheFile: /data/sso/tokens.json
copy:
  target:
    type: s3
    s3:
      {
        endpoint: https://s3.example.com,
        bucket: holtdroid,
        prefix: work,
        accessKey: env:S3_ACCESS_KEY,
        secretKey: env:S3_SECRET_KEY,
      }
notify:
  urls: [env:NOTIFY_URL] # e.g. slack://xoxb:<bot token>@C0123ABCD
```

```yaml
# Holtdroid
sources:
  - name: work
    type: s3
    readOnly: true
    s3:
      {
        endpoint: https://s3.example.com,
        bucket: holtdroid,
        prefix: work,
        accessKey: env:S3_ACCESS_KEY,
        secretKey: env:S3_SECRET_KEY,
      }
```

### Broker mode

[Section titled “Broker mode”](#broker-mode)

The job serves `GET /credentials` with temporary keys in the [ECS container credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-container-credentials.html) format, behind a token. Holtdroid’s S3 source fetches them through `credentialsURL` and refreshes them before they expire. Nothing is copied, and the `include` rules are applied by the api. While there is no session, the endpoint answers `503`, and the source shows an error instead of its builds.

```yaml
# holtdroid-s3-sync
broker:
  enabled: true
  token: env:BROKER_TOKEN
copy:
  enabled: false
```

```yaml
# Holtdroid
sources:
  - name: work
    type: s3
    readOnly: true
    include: ["/releases/*", "!/releases/night/*"]
    s3:
      endpoint: https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com
      region: eu-west-1
      bucket: work-apks
      prefix: android
      credentialsURL: http://holtdroid-s3-sync:8080/credentials
      credentialsToken: env:BROKER_TOKEN
```

Any other service that speaks the same format can serve these credentials.

### Permissions

[Section titled “Permissions”](#permissions)

The permission set, or the keys, needs `s3:ListBucket` on the bucket for the prefix and `s3:GetObject` on its objects. Nothing writes to the source bucket.

# Slack

> Copy APKs posted in Slack channels, threads and forwards into a source with holtdroid-slack-sync.

Holtdroid doesn’t talk to Slack itself. [holtdroid-slack-sync](https://github.com/holtdroid/holtdroid-sync/blob/main/docs/slack.md) is a separate, stateless job that polls channels and writes every `.apk` it finds, with a [`.meta.json` sidecar](/sources/overview/#the-metajson-sidecar), into a folder or S3 prefix that the api lists as a read-only source.

It picks up APKs:

* attached to channel messages;
* in thread replies;
* inside forwarded messages.

Optionally it announces new builds the same way as the other sync jobs: one message per pass through [shoutrrr](https://github.com/nicholas-fedor/shoutrrr) (Slack, Telegram, Discord, Matrix, ntfy, email, webhooks, …). The message lists each build’s name, version, package and size, a link to the Slack message, and two [launch links](/sources/overview/#launch-links):

* **Quick launch** starts a device right away with the user’s last provider and location;
* **Launch** opens the launch dialog.

## 1. Create the Slack app

[Section titled “1. Create the Slack app”](#1-create-the-slack-app)

The quickest way is to create it from the manifest:

1. Open <https://api.slack.com/apps> → **Create New App** → **From a manifest**, and pick the workspace.
2. Paste the manifest below, then click **Create** → **Install to Workspace**.
3. Copy the **Bot User OAuth Token** (`xoxb-…`) from **OAuth & Permissions**.

slack-app-manifest.yaml

```yaml
display_information:
  name: Holtdroid
  description: Copies APKs posted here into Holtdroid and announces them with launch links.
  background_color: "#8a5a3c"
features:
  bot_user:
    display_name: Holtdroid
    always_online: false
oauth_config:
  scopes:
    bot:
      - channels:history
      - groups:history
      - files:read
      - users:read
      - chat:write
settings:
  org_deploy_enabled: false
  socket_mode_enabled: false
  token_rotation_enabled: false
```

| Scope                                | Needed for                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `channels:history`, `groups:history` | reading public / private channels                      |
| `files:read`                         | downloading the APKs                                   |
| `users:read`                         | uploader names (optional; without it you see user IDs) |
| `chat:write`                         | announcements into Slack (optional)                    |

Manifests can’t set the app icon, so upload it under **Basic Information** if you want one, e.g. [`assets/holtdroid-icon.png`](https://github.com/holtdroid/holtdroid-sync/blob/main/assets/holtdroid-icon.png).

Then invite the bot to every channel: `/invite @Holtdroid`. Channels are configured by ID, e.g. `C0123ABCD`: open the channel details and find the ID at the bottom of **About**.

## 2. Deploy the job

[Section titled “2. Deploy the job”](#2-deploy-the-job)

The chart is in the sync repository (`deploy/helm/holtdroid-sync`, and `oci://ghcr.io/holtdroid/charts/holtdroid-sync` for tagged releases); `job` picks the Slack sync:

```yaml
job: slack
existingSecret: holtdroid-slack-sync # SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, S3_ACCESS_KEY, S3_SECRET_KEY, NOTIFY_URL
config:
  slack:
    token: env:SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
    channels: [C0123ABCD]
  target:
    type: s3
    s3:
      endpoint: https://s3.example.com
      region: us-east-1
      bucket: holtdroid
      prefix: slack
      accessKey: env:S3_ACCESS_KEY
      secretKey: env:S3_SECRET_KEY
  notify: # optional: announce new builds
    urls: [env:NOTIFY_URL] # e.g. slack://xoxb:<bot token without xoxb->@C0123ABCD
    portalURL: https://holtdroid.example.com
    source: slack
```

To announce into the channel itself, reuse the bot token in the shoutrrr URL. Builds whose message is older than `notify.maxAge` (24 hours by default) aren’t announced, so the first pass over `lookback` stays quiet.

Every key can also come from `HOLTDROID_SLACK_SYNC_*` environment variables, e.g. `HOLTDROID_SLACK_SYNC_SLACK__CHANNELS=C1,C2`. The full reference is in the job’s [docs](https://github.com/holtdroid/holtdroid-sync/blob/main/docs/slack.md#configuration).

## 3. Add the source to Holtdroid

[Section titled “3. Add the source to Holtdroid”](#3-add-the-source-to-holtdroid)

Point a read-only source at the same place. Its `name` has to match `notify.source`, or the launch links open the wrong source:

```yaml
sources:
  - name: slack
    type: s3
    readOnly: true
    s3:
      endpoint: https://s3.example.com
      region: us-east-1
      bucket: holtdroid
      prefix: slack
      accessKey: env:S3_ACCESS_KEY
      secretKey: env:S3_SECRET_KEY
```

## What ends up in the source

[Section titled “What ends up in the source”](#what-ends-up-in-the-source)

```plaintext
{channel ID}/{file ID}/{file name}.apk
{channel ID}/{file ID}/{file name}.apk.meta.json
```

| Sidecar field  | Value                                                                                   |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `changelog`    | the message text; for a forward, the forwarder’s comment and then the original message  |
| `note`, `link` | permalink of the message in the channel                                                 |
| `uploadedBy`   | display name of whoever posted it (bots: the bot’s name; forwards: the original author) |
| `uploadedAt`   | message time (forwards: the original message’s time)                                    |
| `title`        | the Slack file title, if it differs from the file name                                  |
| `origin`       | `slack`                                                                                 |

It also writes `{file name}.apk.icon.png`, the launcher icon re-rendered at 256 px, when one can be extracted.

## How it polls

[Section titled “How it polls”](#how-it-polls)

Each pass reads the history of the last `lookback` (7 days by default) and lists the source. Only files the source doesn’t have yet get downloaded, so a restart loses nothing and does no extra work. A thread is fetched again only when it has a new reply. Edits to a top-level message rewrite its sidecar; the APK isn’t downloaded again.

Polling has these limits:

* replies to threads whose parent is older than `lookback` are missed;
* edits to thread replies that are already synced show up only after the thread gets another reply.

# Local development

> Toolchain and day-to-day commands for working on Holtdroid.

The toolchain is pinned in `mise.toml`: Go, Bun, golangci-lint and Helm.

```sh
mise install
bun install
```

| Command        | What it does                                                 |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `make check`   | Everything CI runs                                           |
| `make test`    | `go test -race ./...`                                        |
| `make lint`    | golangci-lint, `tsc`, oxlint, oxfmt check                    |
| `make fmt`     | Format Go and TypeScript                                     |
| `make openapi` | Regenerate the UI’s API clients from the Go contracts        |
| `make build`   | Build the UI and `bin/holtdroid` with it embedded            |
| `make docs`    | Build this site into `docs/dist`                             |
| `make dev`     | Run `holtdroid dev` on `:8080`                               |
| `make web-dev` | Run the Vite dev server, proxying `/api` and `/s` to `:8080` |

## Running without a cluster

[Section titled “Running without a cluster”](#running-without-a-cluster)

`holtdroid dev` starts the portal with anonymous sign-in, a read-only artifact source named `local` that lists the APKs in a directory, a writable `uploads` source for the Upload button, and a `fake` device provider whose devices boot in a few seconds, stream a short recorded screen and serve a placeholder DevTools page. Nothing else is needed:

```sh
make dev                     # or: go run ./cmd/holtdroid dev --apks ~/Downloads
make web-dev                 # in a second terminal, then open http://localhost:5173
```

Useful flags: `--apks <dir>`, `--uploads <dir>` (default: a temporary directory), `--slots 4`, `--step-delay 2s`, `--idle-timeout 30m`, `--cache <dir>`, `--no-direct` and `--default-location de` (fake VPN locations).

It also runs the SSH gateway on `--ssh :2222` with temporary host and authority keys and serves the client builds from `bin/connect` (`--connect-clients`, built by `make connect`), so the Computers page’s command connects your machine to the fake devices. Their ADB is the fake provider’s small adbd, and their published ports are local listeners.

Frontend tooling runs on Bun. Type checking uses TypeScript 7 (the native compiler); linting and formatting use oxlint and oxfmt.

Contributor-facing design notes live in [`design/`](https://github.com/holtdroid/holtdroid/tree/main/design), and the rules for humans and coding agents in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/holtdroid/holtdroid/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

# Holtdroid WebView

> A WebView test browser with DevTools unlocked, presets, several engines and live control over adb.

[Holtdroid WebView](https://github.com/holtdroid/holtdroid-webview) is a small Android app for testing web pages inside a WebView. It is made for Holtdroid sessions but works on any phone or emulator on its own.

It opens a page in the system WebView (or GeckoView), lets you change how the WebView is set up, and keeps remote debugging on, so every page shows up in Holtdroid’s DevTools tab and in `chrome://inspect`. Settings are grouped into presets on the start screen, and everything — presets, single settings and actions like resize or freeze — can be driven from adb while the page is open.

## Install

[Section titled “Install”](#install)

Releases are on [GitHub](https://github.com/holtdroid/holtdroid-webview/releases):

| File                                              | What                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `holtdroid-webview-<version>.apk`                 | WebView and Custom Tabs, about 2 MB, any ABI       |
| `holtdroid-webview-gecko-<version>-x86_64.apk`    | plus GeckoView, for emulators (Holtdroid sessions) |
| `holtdroid-webview-gecko-<version>-arm64-v8a.apk` | plus GeckoView, for phones                         |

Both builds use the package name `io.github.holtdroid.webview`, so installing one replaces the other. In Holtdroid, upload the APK or publish it into a source (for example with the [GitHub sync](/sources/github/)) and launch it like any other app; through [ADB](/concepts/adb/) `adb install -r holtdroid-webview-<version>.apk` works too.

## The start screen

[Section titled “The start screen”](#the-start-screen)

* **Open a page**: type an address or a search and pick the preset to open it with. Recent addresses sit under the field.
* **Engines**: the active WebView provider with its version. Tap it to see the installed providers and copy the command that switches between them.
* **Presets**: tap a card to open its start address (or the address you typed) with its settings. The menu edits, duplicates, reorders, deletes a preset or makes it the default for links and adb. Tags on the card summarise what the preset changes; the risky ones are red.
* The top bar switches the theme (system, light, dark) and opens app settings: Material You colours, external control on/off, restoring the built-in presets, clearing every engine’s data.
* **Documentation** opens this page.

The built-in presets:

| Preset       | What it does                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Browse       | A plain browser window: toolbar, strict TLS, DevTools on                                                                    |
| Unlocked     | TLS errors ignored, mixed content, file access, popups, permissions granted, Eruda, autoplay, screen kept on                |
| Kiosk        | Full screen without browser UI, navigation locked to the start host, Back opens the controls, no zoom, popups or long press |
| App shell    | Edge to edge like an app’s own WebView, with a floating handle                                                              |
| Small phone  | A 360 × 640 viewport framed in the middle of the screen                                                                     |
| Desktop site | Desktop user agent, overview viewport, landscape                                                                            |
| Fresh start  | Wipes cookies, storage, cache and history on every launch, no HTTP cache                                                    |
| Proxy        | All traffic through `127.0.0.1:8080` with TLS errors ignored                                                                |

The Proxy preset fits Holtdroid’s [connected computers](/concepts/ssh/): run mitmproxy or Charles on port 8080 of your computer, publish that port on the Computers page and watch the traffic. User-installed CA certificates are trusted too, so a strict preset also works once the proxy’s CA is installed on the device.

## The page

[Section titled “The page”](#the-page)

In Standard and Immersive mode a toolbar shows back, the address (tap to edit), the keyboard button, reload and the controls button. Edge-to-edge and Kiosk modes hide it; the floating handle (draggable) opens the controls instead. Back goes back in history and then to the start screen, or opens the controls when **Back opens controls** is on.

The control panel holds:

* **Freeze**: pauses timers, animations and rendering of the page and blocks input until you resume. Useful to inspect a transient state in DevTools.
* **Hard reload**: clears the HTTP cache and reloads.
* **Desktop**: toggles the desktop user agent and overview mode.
* **Dark**: switches the app theme; pages see it through `prefers-color-scheme`.
* **Console**: messages the page logged, and a prompt that evaluates JavaScript in the page.
* **Eruda**: injects the [Eruda](https://github.com/liriliri/eruda) in-page DevTools. Eruda is bundled into the APK and injected the way DevTools runs scripts, so it works offline and on pages with a strict Content Security Policy (only its icon font may be blocked there).
* **Keyboard**: shows or hides the on-screen keyboard for the focused field (see below).
* **Rotate** and **Settings**: swap the frame’s width and height; edit every setting of the open page, apply it, or save it as a preset.
* **Display**: the display mode and the toolbar position.
* **Viewport**: frame presets from 320 × 568 to 1280 × 800, and the scale. The badge under a framed page shows its size in CSS pixels and its scale.
* **Clear data**: cache, cookies, storage or everything.
* **DevTools**: remote debugging on/off and the `adb forward` command for the page’s DevTools socket.
* **Engine**: WebView, GeckoView or a Custom Tab.

## On-screen keyboard

[Section titled “On-screen keyboard”](#on-screen-keyboard)

Android hides the on-screen keyboard while a hardware keyboard is attached. Holtdroid’s emulators report one (`hw.keyboard=yes`), so tapping a field there brings up no keyboard; you type through the session’s keyboard instead. To get the on-screen one, focus the field and press the keyboard button. If the system still hides it, the app shows two fixes:

```sh
# show the on-screen keyboard next to a hardware one, for every app
adb shell settings put secure show_ime_with_hard_keyboard 1


# or let the app switch that setting on by itself when you press the button
adb shell pm grant io.github.holtdroid.webview android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
```

The same setting is **Use on-screen keyboard** in the system’s physical keyboard settings, which the dialog opens.

## Engines

[Section titled “Engines”](#engines)

* **WebView** is Android’s system WebView. Android uses one provider for every app, and only the system can change it: run `adb shell cmd webviewupdate set-webview-implementation <package>` (the Engines dialog copies it for each installed provider), or use Developer options → WebView implementation. Holtdroid’s [device card](/concepts/adb/) switches it too.
* **GeckoView** is Firefox’s engine, built into the `-gecko` APK. Settings marked “WebView only” don’t apply to it; the console can’t evaluate scripts. Debug it from Firefox on a computer: `about:debugging` → USB devices.
* **Custom Tab** opens the page in the default browser’s Custom Tab, which shares that browser’s cookies. None of the app’s settings apply there.

## Settings

[Section titled “Settings”](#settings)

Every setting has a key. The editor shows it under the description, and the same key works in adb commands and in the `holtdroid-webview://` link. Booleans take `true`/`false` (also `1`/`0`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`), choices are case-insensitive, numbers are plain integers.

| Key                    | Values                                          | Default                   | What                                                        |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`                  | address                                         | `https://www.google.com/` | Start address                                               |
| `engine`               | `webview` `gecko` `custom-tabs`                 | `webview`                 | Engine                                                      |
| `display`              | `standard` `immersive` `edge` `kiosk`           | `standard`                | Display mode                                                |
| `toolbar`              | `top` `bottom`                                  | `top`                     | Toolbar position                                            |
| `handle`               | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Floating handle when the toolbar is hidden                  |
| `lockBack`             | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Back opens the controls instead of leaving                  |
| `orientation`          | `auto` `portrait` `landscape` `locked`          | `auto`                    | Orientation lock (`locked` keeps the current one)           |
| `keepScreenOn`         | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Keep the screen on                                          |
| `width`, `height`      | dp, `0` = fill                                  | `0`                       | Viewport frame                                              |
| `scale`                | percent, `0` = fit                              | `0`                       | Frame scale                                                 |
| `javaScript`           | boolean                                         | `true`                    | JavaScript                                                  |
| `domStorage`           | boolean                                         | `true`                    | localStorage and sessionStorage                             |
| `zoom`                 | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Pinch to zoom                                               |
| `zoomControls`         | boolean                                         | `false`                   | On-screen zoom buttons                                      |
| `wideViewport`         | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Honour `<meta name=viewport>`                               |
| `overviewMode`         | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Fit the page width to the screen                            |
| `textZoom`             | 25–400                                          | `100`                     | Text size, percent                                          |
| `darkening`            | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Algorithmic darkening of light pages in the dark theme      |
| `mediaAutoplay`        | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Play media without a gesture                                |
| `blockImages`          | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Don’t load images                                           |
| `offline`              | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Block every network load                                    |
| `cacheMode`            | `default` `no-cache` `cache-first` `cache-only` | `default`                 | HTTP cache                                                  |
| `userAgent`            | `default` `desktop` `custom`                    | `default`                 | User agent                                                  |
| `customUserAgent`      | text                                            |                           | Used with `userAgent=custom`                                |
| `userAgentSuffix`      | text                                            |                           | Appended to the user agent                                  |
| `headers`              | `Name: value` lines                             |                           | Extra headers on loads you start (not on subresources)      |
| `proxy`                | `host:port` or `scheme://host:port`             |                           | Proxy for all WebView traffic                               |
| `proxyBypass`          | hosts, comma separated                          |                           | Hosts that skip the proxy                                   |
| `ssl`                  | `strict` `ask` `ignore`                         | `strict`                  | TLS certificate errors                                      |
| `mixedContent`         | `never` `compatible` `always`                   | `compatible`              | http resources on https pages                               |
| `safeBrowsing`         | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Safe Browsing                                               |
| `cookies`              | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Cookies                                                     |
| `thirdPartyCookies`    | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Third-party cookies                                         |
| `permissions`          | `ask` `grant` `deny`                            | `ask`                     | Camera, microphone and location requests                    |
| `allowedHosts`         | hosts, comma separated                          |                           | Pages may only navigate to these hosts and their subdomains |
| `externalApps`         | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Follow `tel:`, `mailto:`, `intent:`, `market:` links        |
| `popups`               | boolean                                         | `false`                   | `window.open` and `target=_blank` (opened in the same view) |
| `jsDialogs`            | boolean                                         | `true`                    | `alert`, `confirm`, `prompt`, `beforeunload`                |
| `longPress`            | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Text selection and context menu                             |
| `fileAccess`           | boolean                                         | `false`                   | `file://` URLs                                              |
| `universalFileAccess`  | boolean                                         | `false`                   | `file://` pages may read anything                           |
| `contentAccess`        | boolean                                         | `true`                    | `content://` URLs                                           |
| `clearOnStart`         | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Wipe all data whenever the page opens                       |
| `debugging`            | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Remote debugging                                            |
| `eruda`                | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Inject the bundled Eruda                                    |
| `console`              | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Keep console messages                                       |
| `userScript`           | JavaScript                                      |                           | Injected at document start into every frame                 |
| `hardwareAcceleration` | boolean                                         | `true`                    | Off renders in software                                     |
| `offscreenPreRaster`   | boolean                                         | `false`                   | Draw tiles outside the viewport ahead of time               |

`allowedHosts` limits navigation the page starts; addresses you load yourself (the address bar, `cmd=load`) always open.

## Control from adb

[Section titled “Control from adb”](#control-from-adb)

The app listens to two entry points:

* `am start` opens a page, starting the app if needed.
* `am broadcast` acts on the page that is open now. The app must be running. The broadcast prints the result: `result=-1` means success, `result=1` an error, and `data` carries the message or the requested value.

Every command is also logged under the `HoltdroidWebView` tag (`adb logcat -s HoltdroidWebView`).

```sh
P=io.github.holtdroid.webview


# open with the default preset
adb shell am start -n $P/.MainActivity -d https://example.com


# open with a preset (id or name) and overrides
adb shell am start -n $P/.MainActivity --es preset unlocked --es url https://example.com \
  --es display kiosk --ez keepScreenOn true


# change settings of the open page
adb shell am broadcast -a $P.CONTROL -p $P --es ssl ignore --es userAgent desktop


# resize the viewport, then back to full size
adb shell am broadcast -a $P.CONTROL -p $P --es cmd resize --es size 390x844
adb shell am broadcast -a $P.CONTROL -p $P --es cmd resize


# run JavaScript and print the result (quote the whole command for the device shell)
adb shell "am broadcast -a $P.CONTROL -p $P --es cmd eval --es js 'document.title'"
```

`--es`, `--ei` and `--ez` all work; values are converted to the setting’s type. Commands go in `cmd`; without one, `am start` opens a page and `am broadcast` applies the settings to the open page.

| `cmd`                                 | Arguments                                    | What                                                                |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`                                | `preset`, `url`, any setting                 | Open a page with a preset (default preset if omitted) and overrides |
| `set`                                 | any setting, `url`                           | Change settings of the open page; `url` also loads it               |
| `load`                                | `url`                                        | Load an address in the open page                                    |
| `resize`                              | `width`, `height` or `size=WxH`, `scale`     | Frame the viewport; no arguments returns to full size               |
| `rotate`                              |                                              | Swap width and height                                               |
| `freeze`, `unfreeze`, `toggle-freeze` |                                              | Pause or resume the page                                            |
| `reload`                              | `hard=true`                                  | Reload, optionally clearing the HTTP cache first                    |
| `back`, `forward`, `stop`             |                                              | Navigation                                                          |
| `home`                                |                                              | Close the page and return to the start screen                       |
| `clear`                               | `what=cache\|cookies\|storage\|history\|all` | Clear data (default `all`)                                          |
| `eval`                                | `js`                                         | Evaluate JavaScript; prints the JSON result                         |
| `console`                             | `lines` (default 50)                         | Print the latest console messages                                   |
| `theme`                               | `theme=system\|light\|dark`                  | Switch the app theme                                                |
| `keyboard`                            | `show=true\|false`                           | Show, hide or toggle the on-screen keyboard for the focused field   |
| `state`                               |                                              | Print the screen, page, viewport and every setting as JSON          |
| `presets`                             |                                              | Print preset ids and names                                          |

Links do the same: `holtdroid-webview://<cmd>?<key>=<value>&…` opens the app and runs the command, for example `holtdroid-webview://open?preset=kiosk&url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com`. The app is also offered as a browser for `http` and `https` links, which then open with the default preset.

Any app on the device can send these broadcasts and links. Turn **External control** off in app settings to accept only plain `url` links.

## DevTools

[Section titled “DevTools”](#devtools)

With `debugging` on, the WebView exposes the DevTools socket `webview_devtools_remote_<pid>`. In a Holtdroid session it appears in the DevTools target list like any other app’s WebView (see [WebView DevTools](/concepts/devtools/)). On your own computer:

```sh
adb forward tcp:9222 localabstract:webview_devtools_remote_$(adb shell pidof io.github.holtdroid.webview)
```

then open `chrome://inspect`, or `http://localhost:9222/json`. The control panel copies the exact command.
